quotes.why: Chökyi Gyaltsen's own mtha' dpyod runs the identical inference — middle wheel, therefore principally teaches ultimate truth — as a premise he accepts, which shows the paragraph is attacking the definition and not the Saṃdhinirmocana pervasion. Found by direct search.
Chökyi Gyaltsen distinguishing what the middle wheel says in its words from what it establishes implicitly — the distinction the opponent's definition collapses. Found by direct search.
The full Saṃdhinirmocana sentence the paragraph abbreviates to five syllables, quoted by Gyaltsab Je at exactly this point in the Ornament's opening. Found by direct search.

Gyaltsab Je noting that on Asaṅga's literal reading of the same sūtra the Prajñāpāramitā sūtras themselves come out provisional — the cost of taking the Saṃdhinirmocana as a definition rather than a description. Found by direct search.
Khedrup Je citing the same Saṃdhinirmocana line in the same commentarial place, to fix which wheel is the 'wheel of no characteristics'.

Tsongkhapa adopting Dharmamitra's division of the Mother's subject matter into ultimate truth and the stages of realization, which is what makes the opponent's reason so easy to establish for the Heart Sūtra. Found by direct search.
The lemma of Haribhadra's on which this whole ཆོས་འཁོར excursus hangs, and the nearest thing the Indian commentary has to a place for it. Found by direct search.
The root-verse line — the Sages' teaching of the various scriptures — that this excursus on the wheel of Dharma is attached to. Found by direct search.
Dharmamitra saying in so many words that the Heart Sūtra is among the texts making ultimate truth their principal subject: the paragraph's reason, stated by an Indian commentator on the Ornament.

Jamyang Zhepa citing Tsongkhapa's Drang nges rnam 'byed that the Heart Sūtra is provisional precisely because it does not attach the ultimate qualifier — the reading the opponent's definition contradicts.
The Svātantrika criterion in full: within the middle wheel, attaching the ultimate qualifier to the object of negation is what makes a sūtra definitive, not the truth it principally treats.
